scope: Eleven preference selectors use the existing Rust SelectState, Rust select layout/display-list and shared-context Metal renderer. Native Views Combobox controls remain the Views baseline. Native window/input/focus/AX/menu and browser preference/domain services remain adapters. Remaining switches/buttons/forms/container ownership are not migrated by this change.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Committed archive with explicit prototype overrides, including page_dialogs.cc/h, and unchanged shared-service install/stage hooks, excluding concurrent root network-policy work. Final staging idempotent and Ninja no-work.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

verification.standalone_editor_model_tests_scope: The 61-case editor model is included in the fresh Rust suite. Separate standalone run not repeated; editor source unchanged.
verification.python_live_scope: Two concurrent network/staging tests are outside this UI commit.

additional_performance_scenario_coverage.purpose: Execute all four opt-in performance scenarios as additional automated coverage, with their default 30 trials. Metal validation is enabled; these are not controlled CPU/GPU/drawable presentation comparisons.

coverage: Actual Cocoa digit key after a valid unsupported native font size (17 px): blank selection stays blank until user input chooses 20 px; preference write reaches the selected profile only. Native Combobox baseline and Rust adapter are both exercised.

Site type changes rebuild valid policy choices, reset to Default and reject an out-of-range Ask choice. Save writes the owning profile only. Clear-period selection reaches the original confirmation path; cancellation does not delete data.
All eleven opt-in selectors have no native Combobox/Label child control and expose the combo-box-select accessibility role. Theme and compact category choices use the same Rust control.
Nested preference scrolling hides offscreen Metal surfaces and restores clipped screen bounds when scrolled back. Theme inheritance and hide/reopen are exercised.
Duplicate search provider labels retain keyword identity. Replacing a provider keyword during a pressed interaction cancels the old target; a hidden control cannot change the default provider.

Fresh Rust tests verify clearing a selection invalidates old popup tokens and prefix state, leaves no false selected key, safely admits the first matching option and handles empty/disabled/nonmatching input without usize overflow.
contracts: Programmatic preference refresh leaves unchanged selection/models untouched, preserving the active prefix/menu. In the Rust adapter, provider key or label changes replace the model and invalidate its popup generation. A profile transition cancels preference picker interactions before resynchronization.
Nil selection remains distinct from option zero for supported Chromium values outside the preset list.
Site policy replacements preserve original native behavior: the new model starts at Default. All actual writes, authorization, managed-preference checks, scope and persistence remain native services.

initial_compile_issue.issue: SceneSelect callback setter name hid a virtual Button callback overload under -Woverloaded-virtual. Renamed it SetChangedCallback; no API behavior change.

preferred_size_compile_issue.issue: Direct PreferredSizeChanged access is protected in pinned Views; keep public InvalidateLayout and enable ScrollView preferred-content sizing instead. No GUI run from that failed build.

initial_gate_investigation.native_empty_choice: Actual Cocoa input on a nonempty native Combobox model with null selection hit its existing OnKeyPressed CHECK. The project-local PreferenceCombobox keeps the real native model/prefix/AX/menu services and bypasses only this invalid guard path; no replacement value or shadow editing model is introduced.
initial_gate_investigation.site_fixture: NavigateBoth leaves personal selected. The initial site-rule test incorrectly assumed work was active; both backends correctly wrote the active personal profile. The corrected test explicitly selects work before checking isolation.
initial_gate_investigation.scroll_surface: The initial Metal test expected ScrollRectToVisible to hide an earlier field. Follow-up geometry proved the earlier field was still natively visible, so this alone did not establish stale GPU state. Driving the native scrollbar showed an underestimated content extent (534 px despite later overflowing fields, with only 18 px scroll range). Enable ScrollView contents preferred sizing so the existing layout invalidation after filtering remeasures the scroll layer extent on both backends. The final test verifies actual native viewport exclusion before GPU visibility, and both-backend coverage requires the last font editor to remain reachable. Preferences also use Chromium ScopedScrollSynchronizer and explicit viewport callbacks for native-overlay coherence.
initial_gate_investigation.native_resize_scroll_race: After the extent fix, all 37 Metal cases passed but the native last-field test still attempted compositor scrolling immediately after resizing the layer. Pinned Layer::SetScrollOffset documents that scrolling before the resized layer commits may not complete. The final fixture focuses the actual panel and awaits RequestSuccessfulPresentationTimeForNextFrame before scrolling. It retains strict actual viewport reachability assertions; no sleep, disabled animation or synthetic geometry success is substituted.

limits: The modal/frame/row/container/switch/button and native event/focus/AX nodes still have remaining Views ownership. This is selector migration, not complete preferences or full UI parity.
Actual native popup/candidate-window/VoiceOver/complex bidi/scale/trackpad/GPU-recovery/focus/menu acceptance remains distinct from reducer/domain and automated Cocoa input evidence.
Default performance scenarios add execution coverage with Metal validation enabled. No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup is claimed.
Real-user Arc import and interactive manual window are excluded per backend. Normal installed apps/profiles are untouched. No bundle was packaged or signed.
No new crate/library/dependency/license. Apache-2.0 release/upstream notice verification remains a release check.
